reviewedInputs.officialSourceSection: C8 Lernbereich 3: comparison of CO2 balance and reaction heat when burning different fuels

findings.detail: The current German/English goal and the official C8.3 combustion clause support comparison of direct CO2 and released reaction heat on a consistent basis for each quantity. The profile stays inside direct complete combustion; it requires no whole-life comparison or overall energy-carrier judgment.

Stoichiometric CO2 per mol is 88 g for ethanol and 132 g for propane. With the supplied same-convention teaching heat values, 88/1.37 is about 64 g/MJ and 132/2.22 about 59 g/MJ. The case checks why raw per-mol order cannot answer the equal-heat question; it does not require balancing an equation.

The supplied 0.50 kg hydrogen and 1.00 kg butane samples yield 120 and 46 MJ/kg respectively; direct CO2 is 0 and about 65 g/MJ (3000/46). Zero direct CO2 follows from hydrogen containing no carbon, while the separate upstream rows prevent a claim of total emission freedom or climate neutrality. The rounded butane CO2 figure is compatible with the stoichiometric order of magnitude.

Two data-only cases use different fuel pairs, per-mole versus unequal-mass inputs, and different reasoning traps. Neither can be solved from the active methane/pure-carbon comparison image. The cases are briefs for future independent learner work, not observed demonstrations.

The materialized record is bound to the current direct-combustion DE/EN goal and carries needs_human_review, reviewAuthority ai_candidate, E1/G1, and no reviewRunIds or human/learner claim. The targeted checker reports 1 configured goal, 0 approved, 1 needs human review, and 0 blockers.

nonBlockingQualification: The numbers are explicitly rounded teaching data; each case says its heat figures share one convention. A later task must retain the separate upstream row and direct-only boundary when using the hydrogen case. This QA does not approve a real-world fuel ranking.
